issue_context.title: Using OrderedDict in GroupBy Module(s)
issue_context.body:
Spurred by conversation in https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/25224#discussion_r264786749 right now we are using plain old dictionaries in most of the groupby aggregation functions. For Py35 this makes the order of the returned result non-deterministic.

We could theoretically make a stronger assertion around the order here by replacing those dicts with OrderedDicts
comments: Since I've already been working with this, I will also continue with this issue. I'll make a simple WIP PR right now and will continue working on it. I'm thinking of changing the simple dicts to OrderedDicts in the aggregation functions of groupby and writing some tests in order to test the ordering.

review_comments: For my curiosity, what was the old order for various python versions?

Index(['max', 'mean', 'min', 'ohlc', 'sum'], dtype='object'). This would have been the result in all python versions previous to the changes I made in concat (#25224). After the changes, this would have been the return for the versions below Python 3.6, and the order observed in this PR for 3.6 and above. This is why we converted dicts to OrderedDicts in the aggregation functions, to ensure that result would be consistent in all versions.
